A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-NES research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original OpenFWI evaluations, 3D scalability results, and equivariance, pretraining, and fitting-budget analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 reports the retained experiments plus original Functa comparisons, spherical evaluations, architectural ablations, and empirical steerability tests.

M1.justification: The backbone, cross-attention construction, training losses, and fitting algorithms are retained. Section 3.2 introduces an optional discrete-semimetric factor with a straight-through estimator for general group actions, providing a limited procedural extension. Its use in the reported experiments is not established.

E1.justification: V2 extends the Euclidean 2D and extruded-3D coverage to spherical constant-speed, projected Style-B, and Gaussian-obstacle fields (Section 5.3 and Appendix D.3). Evaluation on curved geometry and obstacle-avoiding spherical paths adds substantive domain and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Functa as an evaluated comparator on five B-type OpenFWI datasets in Table 2. Its underlying work was cited but not benchmarked in v1. The FC-DeepONet and FMM comparisons remain; newly reported FC-DeepONet timing does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: V2 adds spherical evaluation using Hamiltonian FMM references, matched Functa settings with 100 fitting epochs, and controlled embedding and latent-configuration experiments. Appendix D.1 also revises the stated 2D attention-head count from three to two and corrects a validation/testing label. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses compare MLP, polynomial, and RFF embeddings; vary latent number and dimensionality; and empirically test rotation/translation steerability (Appendices E.3, E.4, and E.7). Figure 4 adds spherical path-planning cases with and without obstacles. Earlier equivariance, pretraining, and fitting-budget analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original OpenFWI accuracy entries remain unchanged, including v1 Table 2 retained as v2 Table 4. V2 adds Functa, spherical, architectural-ablation, and steerability findings; Table 3 reports spherical RE values of 0.013 and 0.015. Table 1 adds approximately 0.615 seconds for FC-DeepONet, and the reported backbone parameter count changes from 64,895 to 648,965.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 formally introduces an invariant-semimetric requirement for the distance factor. Appendix A corrects the inverse-differential evaluation point and squared-norm expressions in the isometric proof. The principal steered-solution and latent-pose-extension results retain their substantive conclusions.

C1.justification: The central ENF generalization and grid-free Eikonal-solver contributions remain. The abstract and introduction expand the empirical-validation claim to spherical benchmarks, while the conclusion extends the performance comparison to conditional neural fields represented by Functa.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of embedding efficiency and the balance between spatial latent coverage and context expressivity. Appendix F.3 explains weaker FlatVel-A/B performance through supervision and discretization biases, while F.2 develops reinforcement-learning and multi-input similarity applications. The earlier conditional-versus-unconditional discussion is largely retained in F.1.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code URL and states that result-generation scripts are included. It adds Functa architecture details and spherical latent configurations, sampling distributions, interpolation, and reference-solver information. It also corrects the parameter count and clarifies that reported fitting times cover all 100 test fields, correcting v1's per-field description.

R1.justification: Related work more explicitly positions product-manifold inputs and completeness guarantees against prior ENFs. New citations support straight-through estimation, SIRENs, Hamiltonian FMM, and reinforcement-learning/test-time-scaling connections; Bellaard et al. (2023) is removed. These changes refine the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites portions of related work and the conclusion, expands background and loss explanations, and adds an appendix contents page. The former E.5 discussion becomes F.1 within a larger discussion section. The overall section sequence and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds four tables for Functa, spherical performance, and architectural ablations, plus spherical-path and empirical-steerability figures. Figure 1 gains clearer labels, and timing captions specify 100-field totals. Existing benchmark tables and plots are largely retained and renumbered; some E-NES scores are redisplayed alongside new comparisons.

improvement.justification: The spherical experiments address v1's lack of non-Euclidean empirical validation for a central claim. Functa comparisons and targeted ablations substantially strengthen assessment of the geometric-conditioning contribution. Corrected timing scope, added comparator latency, parameter-count corrections, and code access information also improve transparency and reproducibility, making accuracy-versus-cost tradeoffs easier to assess.
